rows.comment: Section label that says what the control sets.
Validation message that tells the reader what to do.
Format string for name and time.
"Separated itself" is a figure of speech. Say that no link was found.
lineComments: Personified phrasing replaced with the actual state.

rows.comment: "Cleared the bar" is a metaphor for an unstated threshold. State the comparison and the result.
lineComments: Names the four outcomes compared and replaces "cleared the bar" with the result.
rows.replacement: Each item you log is compared with your recovery, HRV, resting heart rate and sleep efficiency. None has shown a difference yet.

rows.comment: Em dash and an aphoristic second sentence. The caveat (association, not causation) is worth keeping, stated directly.
lineComments: Drops the em dash and the "kind of day" line; states the confounding mechanism.
rows.replacement: This shows a link in your own days, not a cause. Days when you do something may already differ from other days for other reasons.

rows.comment: Direction word used in a composed sentence.
Direction word used in a composed sentence.
States the count, field, outcome and amount. Placeholders must stay.
Names the statistic and gives the value. The method name must not change; a definition would need a UI change beyond this string.
lineComments: Statistic name with value and interval placeholders.

rows.comment: Em dash, scare quotes and a cute "quietly mean". The caveat is useful; state the limit and the confounder directly.
lineComments: Says what is recorded (time only) and why a later time may also mean more caffeine.
rows.replacement: This records only the time of your last caffeine. Two cups and five look the same, so a later time may also mean more caffeine. A long, stressful day can cause both a late coffee and a poor night.

rows.comment: Thresholds (eight weeks, five per weekday) kept. Wording is clumsy ("weeks of days").
rows.replacement: Comparing weekdays needs at least eight weeks of data, with at least five of each weekday.

rows.comment: "Account for having checked all seven" hides the method. Name it: correction for comparing seven days.
lineComments: Names the multiple-comparison correction and drops "we".
rows.replacement: After correcting for comparing all seven days, no weekday differs from the others.

rows.comment: States the weekday, the metric and the difference from the median.
Em dash and aphorism ("container"). Keep the not-a-cause and not-advice caveats, stated plainly.
lineComments: Replaces the container metaphor with a direct statement; keeps the disclaimer.
rows.replacement: Based on {n} of these days. A weekday does not cause a difference; what you do on it may. This is not advice.

rows.comment: States why there is no night: recordings too short to score.
"Watched" is odd for a band that records data. Use the verb the band does.
Metric label; understandable next to the recorded time.
"We watched" and "the rest is not a measurement" are indirect. Say the band recorded X, the rest has no data, and what is computed from it.
lineComments: Active, concrete; keeps both placeholders and the denominator logic.
rows.replacement: The band recorded {watched} of your {inBed} in bed. The rest has no measurement. Asleep time and the stage shares below use only the recorded time.

rows.comment: States how the window was derived.
"Staged from the signals" is vague and passive. Another string says staging needs movement and beat timing.
lineComments: Names the inputs instead of "the signals".
rows.replacement: This window was detected from movement and beat timing

rows.comment: "Find the edges" and "best guess" are loose. Say what could not be found and that the times are estimates.
rows.replacement: Staging could not find when you fell asleep or woke up, so these times are estimates.

rows.comment: Clumsy fragment. Name the measure (time to fall asleep) and keep the placeholder.
rows.replacement: Time to fall asleep, from the start of your window: {band}.

rows.comment: "You told us" is chatty and "nothing is scored" is passive.
rows.replacement: You marked this stretch as not sleep, so it is not scored.
Undo and go back to automatic

rows.comment: Spelling is British here but "Re-analyze" elsewhere in the app.
Error recovery text worth keeping. Em dash, semicolon and mixed spelling; split into short sentences.
lineComments: Gives both causes, confirms the times are saved, and names the recovery action.
rows.replacement: The night was not re-analyzed. Another re-analysis was already running, or this one failed. The times you set are saved. Re-analyze everything on Your data applies them.

rows.comment: "One was missing" is a punchy fragment with an unclear antecedent.
lineComments: Names both inputs and says one is absent.
rows.replacement: Staging needs both movement and beat timing data. One of them is missing for this night.

rows.comment: Gives the interaction and the cycle count. ICU plural must stay intact.
Gives the interaction, count and average. ICU plural must stay intact.
lineComments: Instruction plus count and average, fine.

rows.comment: Tells the reader what to do.
Keep the 5-minute threshold. "Invisible to a wrist" is a flourish; state the detection limit.
lineComments: Replaces the metaphor with the limit and splits the semicolon.
rows.replacement: No wake-ups of 5 minutes or more. The band cannot detect shorter ones.

rows.comment: Keep the 5-minute threshold and plural block. "Invisible to a wrist" is a flourish.
lineComments: Same plural structure; plain statement of the detection limit.
